question: Basel Tool and Die Company (BTD) makes large industrial pipe wrenches in one of its factories. The marketing department estimates demand for this product during the next 6 months to be: In January, the demand is 430, in February, the demand is 430, in March, the demand is 380, in April, the demand is 450, in May, the demand is 520, in June, the demand is 440. With the current labor force, BTD believes it can make approximately 420 pipe wrenches per month at a cost of $40 per wrench using regular-time production. An additional 80 wrenches per month can be made using overtime production at a cost per wrench of $45. Wrenches can be made in advance and held in inventory for later shipment at a cost of $3 per month per wrench. The monthly demand for wrenches must be satisfied every month. At the end of December (beginning of January) BTD has 10 wrenches in inventory. BTD wants to plan its production, including overtime, and inventory for the next 6 months so as to maximize profit. Assuming the revenue for these wrenches is fixed, the production manager can maximize profit by minimizing the total costs incurred in producing and delivering the wrenches. Find the minimal total cost in dollar. Provide your answer rounded to nearest integar.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "months": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "demand": {1: 430, 2: 430, 3: 380, 4: 450, 5: 520, 6: 440},
    "reg_cost": 40,
    "ot_cost": 45,
    "hold_cost": 3,
    "reg_capacity": 420,
    "ot_capacity": 80,
    "initial_inventory": 10,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    months = d["months"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=months)

    # Regular-time production quantity (wrenches)
    # "it can make approximately 420 pipe wrenches per month at a cost of $40 per wrench"
    model.reg = pyo.Var(
        model.T,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, d["reg_capacity"]),
    )

    # Overtime production quantity (wrenches)
    # "An additional 80 wrenches per month can be made using overtime production at a cost per wrench of $45"
    model.ot = pyo.Var(
        model.T,
        within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers,
        bounds=(0, d["ot_capacity"]),
    )

    # End-of-month inventory (wrenches)
    # "Wrenches can be made in advance and held in inventory for later shipment at a cost of $3 per month per wrench"
    model.inv = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: minimize total production, overtime, and holding cost
    # "the production manager can maximize profit by minimizing the total costs incurred in producing and delivering the wrenches"
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (
            sum(d["reg_cost"] * m.reg[t] for t in m.T)
            + sum(d["ot_cost"] * m.ot[t] for t in m.T)
            + sum(d["hold_cost"] * m.inv[t] for t in m.T)
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Inventory balance: prev_inv + reg[t] + ot[t] - inv[t] = demand[t]
    # "The monthly demand for wrenches must be satisfied every month."
    # "At the end of December (beginning of January) BTD has 10 wrenches in inventory."
    def balance_rule(m, t):
        prev = d["initial_inventory"] if t == months[0] else m.inv[t - 1]
        return prev + m.reg[t] + m.ot[t] - m.inv[t] == d["demand"][t]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

    "demand": {"Jan": 430, "Feb": 430, "Mar": 380, "Apr": 450, "May": 520, "Jun": 440},
    "reg_capacity": 420,
    "ot_capacity": 80,
    "reg_cost": 40,
    "ot_cost": 45,
    "hold_cost": 3,
    "initial_inventory": 10,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["months"], ordered=True)

    # Regular-time production per month
    # "With the current labor force, BTD believes it can make approximately 420 pipe wrenches per month at a cost of $40 per wrench using regular-time production."
    # assumption: NonNegativeReals domain (text silent)
    model.reg = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                        bounds=(0, d["reg_capacity"]))

    # Overtime production per month
    # "An additional 80 wrenches per month can be made using overtime production at a cost per wrench of $45."
    # assumption: NonNegativeReals domain (text silent)
    model.ot = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                       bounds=(0, d["ot_capacity"]))

    # Ending inventory per month
    # "Wrenches can be made in advance and held in inventory for later shipment at a cost of $3 per month per wrench."
    # assumption: NonNegativeReals domain (text silent)
    model.inv = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Inventory balance
    # "The monthly demand for wrenches must be satisfied every month."
    # "At the end of December (beginning of January) BTD has 10 wrenches in inventory."
    def balance_rule(m, t):
        prev = d["initial_inventory"] if t == d["months"][0] else m.inv[d["months"][d["months"].index(t) - 1]]
        return prev + m.reg[t] + m.ot[t] - m.inv[t] == d["demand"][t]
    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # Objective: minimize total production, overtime, and holding cost
    # "the production manager can maximize profit by minimizing the total costs incurred in producing and delivering the wrenches"
    # assumption: holding cost charged on beginning-of-month inventory (initial inventory not charged)
    def obj_rule(m):
        cost = 0
        for t in m.T:
            cost += d["reg_cost"] * m.reg[t]
            cost += d["ot_cost"] * m.ot[t]
            prev = d["initial_inventory"] if t == d["months"][0] else m.inv[d["months"][d["months"].index(t) - 1]]
            cost += d["hold_cost"] * prev
        return cost
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model
